rationale: Recorded the account for receipt 91832b58570e4cc7842cfff4d04836e0, which executes the last boundary the account had left as a limitation: under a partition the restarted node's reconstruction and the committed configuration of its peers each elected a leader in the same term, both committed an entry, and neither side's store held the other's entry, while the flag-disabled control produced a single leader. Added a fact for that split brain, cited the receipt in the support-arithmetic fact, withdrew the limitation that the partition case was untested, and left the discriminator with the remaining store and fault-model boundaries only.

investigations.discriminator: Every consequence this account identified is now exercised, including the partition case. What remains outside is only the surrounding fault and storage model: a disk-backed commit-tracking store, crash and restart timing, a healed partition, and repeated or longer runs. Those are recorded as limitations rather than as open questions.

knowledge.statement: The configuration a node holds decides its own participation and support arithmetic: runFollower declines to campaign when latestIndex is zero or the local ID has no vote in the latest configuration, a candidate needs quorumSize() votes of the latest configuration, and the leader's commitment is constructed from the latest configuration, so a stale or empty reconstruction directly changes which support is required and counted.
knowledge.conditions: The configuration is the one reconstructed at startup or later written by a snapshot install or a configuration change; quorumSize and the commitment are computed from configurations.latest.

knowledge.statement: In the retained partition execution the reconstruction produced two leaders in the same term with disjoint quorums: the restarted node led on its single-voter reconstruction while the two peers it was partitioned from led on the committed three-voter configuration, both sides committed a uniquely named entry (both apply calls returned success), the first side's configuration named one voter against the second side's three, and neither side's log store contained the other side's entry (cross_entries_seen 0), so the cluster held two committed histories. With the flag disabled the same partition left the restarted node unable to lead with only one of the committed configuration's three voters reachable and produced a single leader.
knowledge.conditions: Three-voter committed configuration recorded at log index 106 while the restarted node's snapshot metadata carries a single-voter configuration; the node is disconnected from the other two in both directions with the transport's Disconnect and then stopped and restarted with a fresh empty instance beside it, and the other two keep the committed configuration; the two sides are given up to 800 ms to elect and 1500 ms to commit, and the partition is never healed in the execution.

interpretations.rationale: Receipt 91832b58570e4cc7842cfff4d04836e0 (completed, exit 0, TestAssuranceRestoreCommittedLogsContext passed, 51 parsed events) executes the last boundary. Comparisons 0, 1 and 2 are violated with one valid witness at parsed index 48 (split_inputs at parsed index 47 records the three-voter committed configuration): after the partition the restarted node led on a one-voter reconstruction while the two peers led on the committed three-voter configuration, both in the same term, both committing a uniquely named entry successfully, and neither side's store held the other's entry, so the cluster held two leaders and two committed histories at once; comparison 3 holds at parsed index 50 for the control, where the same partition produced a single leader and the restarted node refused with "node is not the leader". With this receipt the account is complete for the exercised scope, each consequence under its own receipts: the reconstruction diverges from the node's own log in both directions across five shapes because the startup scan starts above max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied) after restoreFromCommittedLogs advanced lastApplied to the tracked commit index [scan_start, restore_lastapplied, cfg_entry]; the wrong context then persists under a live healthy leader until a configuration entry is appended (a1c98fc2bafd4775aa05275dd25f2767); it leaves a sole committed member unable to campaign or contending for a quorum it can never reach; it lets a node acquire leadership and commit with support from a minority of the committed configuration; a client-acknowledged commit then either rests on one copy or is discarded from every store when a majority that never held it forms higher-term leadership; a vote is granted and durably recorded for a peer without a vote, and a peer without a vote acquires leadership on its own initiative; a client membership change replaces the committed configuration with support that is not its majority and demotes its voters; and, when a partition separates the two configurations, both sides lead in the same term and commit divergent histories. No conjecture is left undecided by this account; the remaining limitations are the store, crash, partition-healing and repetition boundaries listed below, and the earlier receipt 0517acf0c7cc4960ab2a9ea0eff68bf0 is recorded as a harness failure in an unrelated case rather than as evidence.
counterevidence: The feature's documented purpose is replaying known-committed logs into the FSM; nothing in the sources makes skipping committed configuration entries a required behaviour, and the existing TestRaft_RestoreCommittedLogs asserts only applied index, tracked commit index and log indices, so it neither exercises nor contradicts the configuration reconstruction.

Competing explanation that the flag's committed-log replay itself, rather than the skipped configuration entry, produces these effects: excluded wherever tested, by the within-flag case whose configuration entry lies above the replayed prefix and by the flag-disabled controls in every receipt, which hold the published configuration and refuse the same requests, decisions, changes and leadership.

Each consequence needs its stated conditions: the partition case needs the two sides physically separated and the restarted side to reach a quorum of its own reconstruction (itself plus the fresh instance); the discard needs the successor leadership to outrank the stale holder's term; the campaign needed the former leader down; the client change needs prevIndex 0 and the committed configuration's voters unreachable. These are the conditions under which the consequences hold, not unconditional effects.

The exercises restart one or two instances at a time in a single process with in-memory transports and stores, and the returning or answering peers were rebuilt with RestoreCommittedLogs disabled unless the case was about their own divergence, so what is exercised is one divergent node's context inside an otherwise correct cluster.
limitations: Single process with in-memory transports and in-memory commit-tracking stores, no crash injection, no disk-backed store and no network fault model beyond the transport's own Disconnect.

Single-shot windows (200-1500 ms depending on the case, 3000 ms for leadership, 1000-1500 ms for commits) and one or two restarted instances per case; no rate, repetition or long-run stability claim follows.
The partition is never healed and no client is served across the healed state, so convergence after healing, membership reconciliation and any data reconciliation are unexercised.

The reconstruction shapes beyond the five exercised ladders, other stores and other configuration flags were not varied; the LogCache entries record a separate startup-plumbing gap rather than a consensus consequence.
